mainTopic: Redeeming an עבד עברי sold to a גוי: רבי's reading of ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ and the ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״ link, and the argument over whether redemption by relatives or by others leads to freedom.
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא in which רבי rules that an עבד עברי sold to a גוי goes free through his relatives' redemption or at the יובל, not after six years. The גמרא first uses רבי's קל וחומר to suggest that he rejects the גזירה שוה of ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that רבי can accept it, because ״יִגְאָלֶנּוּ״ limits redemption by relatives to the slave sold to a גוי. Next, the גמרא brings רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא, who argue about the slave once he is redeemed. רבי יוסי הגלילי says redemption by relatives sets him free, while redemption by others makes him work for the redeemer. רבי עקיבא says the opposite. The גמרא tries to ground their argument in the wording of the פסוק, then in the order of the cases in the פסוק, and finally settles on logic. Strangers would not redeem him if he went free, and a slave would keep selling himself if his relatives always freed him. רבי יוחנן adds that the חכמים, identified as רבי, hold that every redemption sets the slave free. The amud ends as the גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that explains how רבי uses ״וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל״.

steps.title: רבי: The slave sold to a gentile goes free only through his relatives
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק about an עבד עברי sold to a גוי. רבי reads it to mean that this slave is redeemed through his relatives, and not after six years.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And if he is not redeemed by these" — רבי says: through these (relatives) he is redeemed, and he is not redeemed after six years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא where רבי rules that a Jewish slave sold to a גוי does not go free after six years. He goes free only if his relatives redeem him (or at the יובל).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ (by these) points to the relatives listed in the earlier פסוקים. רבי reads it as a limit: this slave's way out is through these relatives, not through the six-year release. The גמרא will soon use this ברייתא as a test case for the ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״ question.

keyTerms.meaning: Is redeemed, meaning set free from slavery
By these, meaning the relatives listed in the פסוק
After six years, the normal release time of an עבד עברי

phrases.english: "And if he is not redeemed by these"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:54. This is about an עבד עברי sold to a גוי.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
Through these he is redeemed,
and he is not redeemed after six.
phrases.notes: "Six" means six years of work, the usual time an עבד עברי goes free.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל בְּאֵלֶּה רַבִּי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test whether רבי learns the גזירה שוה of ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד עברי sold to a גוי is freed through his relatives' redemption, not after six years.

steps.title: רבי's reasoning: a logical argument the verse blocks
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains why the פסוק was needed: a קל וחומר would have said the slave sold to a גוי goes free after six years, so ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ comes to block it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For I might have said: isn't it logical? If the one who cannot be redeemed by relatives (sold to a Jew) goes free after six years, then this one, who can be redeemed by relatives (sold to a גוי), should surely go free after six years too! So the פסוק says "by these": through these he is redeemed, and not after six.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי shows the קל וחומר that the פסוק had to block. This is still part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר goes like this: the slave sold to a Jew has fewer ways out (no redemption by relatives), yet he goes free after six years. So the slave sold to a גוי, who has more ways out, should go free after six years too. The פסוק ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ cuts this off. The key detail for later is the starting point: רבי assumes the slave sold to a Jew cannot be redeemed by relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? This opens a קל וחומר
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger case
The פסוק teaches, which brings the verse that blocks the logic

steps.confusionAlert: Two different slaves are being compared. "One who is not redeemed by these" is the slave sold to a Jew. "This one, who is redeemed by these" is the slave sold to a גוי.

phrases.english: For I could have said: is it not logical?
If one who is not redeemed by these —
phrases.notes: This is the slave sold to a Jew. His relatives cannot buy him out.

phrases.english: is redeemed after six,
this one, who is redeemed by these —
phrases.notes: This is the slave sold to a גוי, whose relatives can redeem him.

phrases.english: is it not logical that he is redeemed after six?
The verse teaches: "by these" —
through these he is redeemed,
and he is not redeemed after six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי needed the פסוק for his ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the פסוק, a קל וחומר would release the slave sold to a גוי after six years. ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ blocks that.

steps.title: Proof that רבי rejects the ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״ link
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues: if רבי learned the גזירה שוה of ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״, the slave sold to a Jew could also be redeemed by relatives, and his קל וחומר would fall apart. So it seems רבי does not learn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think רבי learns "hired worker"–"hired worker," why does he say "If one who is not redeemed by these"? Let him learn "hired worker"–"hired worker" (and then the slave sold to a Jew is redeemed by relatives too)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי's קל וחומר as proof that רבי does not accept the גזירה שוה of ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שָׂכִיר is used for both kinds of עבד עברי, and a גזירה שוה would let each one borrow the other's rules. Then the slave sold to a Jew would borrow redemption by relatives from the slave sold to a גוי. But רבי's קל וחומר assumes the slave sold to a Jew cannot be redeemed by relatives, so רבי must reject the link.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind, used to test a possibility
He learns or derives
Hired worker, a word used in the פסוקים for both kinds of עבד עברי
Linking two topics because the same word appears in both
Why?

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that he derives "hired worker" "hired worker,"
phrases.notes: The word שָׂכִיר appears for both the slave sold to a Jew and the one sold to a גוי, so they could share rules.

phrases.english: why does he say
"If one who is not redeemed by these"?
Let him derive "hired worker" "hired worker"!
phrases.notes: He means: through the link, even the slave sold to a Jew could be redeemed by relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ יָלֵיף שָׂכִיר שָׂכִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference about רבי's view from the starting point of the קל וחומר in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי does not learn the גזירה שוה of ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's קל וחומר assumes the slave sold to a Jew cannot be redeemed by relatives.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: רבי can accept the link, but ״יִגְאָלֶנּוּ״ limits redemption
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof. רבי may accept ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״, but the word ״יִגְאָלֶנּוּ״ (shall redeem him) limits redemption by relatives to the slave sold to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Actually, רבי does learn "hired worker"–"hired worker." But here it is different, because the פסוק says "shall redeem him": him, and not another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof from step 3. He shows that רבי's קל וחומר still works even if רבי accepts the גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה can carry over other rules, but not redemption by relatives. The word ״יִגְאָלֶנּוּ״, "him," limits that rule to the slave sold to a גוי alone. So the slave sold to a Jew still cannot be redeemed by relatives, and רבי's קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really, the opening word of a rejection that keeps the original idea
But here it is different
Shall redeem him
For this one and not for another, a limiting reading of a word

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's ruling does not prove he rejects ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״. Even with the link, ״יִגְאָלֶנּוּ״ keeps redemption by relatives only for the slave sold to a גוי.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Actually, he does derive "hired worker" "hired worker,"
but here it is different,
since the verse says "shall redeem him" —
this one, and not another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְעוֹלָם יָלֵיף שָׂכִיר שָׂכִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove that רבי accepts the גזירה שוה. It only shows the ברייתא fits either view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed the גזירה שוה would carry over redemption by relatives. ״יִגְאָלֶנּוּ״ limits that rule to the slave sold to a גוי.

steps.title: Which תנא disagrees with רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the תנא is who argues on רבי's reading of ״בְּאֵלֶּה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who disagrees with רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא does not read ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ the way רבי does. This sets up the next step, where the answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי used ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ to teach that a slave sold to a גוי is redeemed through relatives and does not go free after six years. The גמרא wants to find the תנאים who use the same word for a different lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time of the משנה
Who disagrees with him

phrases.english: And who is the tanna who disagrees with Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי's reading, the גמרא now looks for the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who argues on רבי's reading of ״בְּאֵלֶּה״.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא argue about freedom or work
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא read ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ as being about whether the redeemed slave goes free or must work for whoever redeemed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא. As a ברייתא teaches about ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל בְּאֵלֶּה״: רבי יוסי הגלילי says that redemption ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ (by relatives) is to freedom, and redemption by anyone else is to work for the redeemer. רבי עקיבא says: redemption ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ is to work for the redeemer, and redemption by anyone else is to freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא disagree with רבי, and quotes a ברייתא where they read ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them use ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ for a different question from רבי's: after he is redeemed, does the slave go fully free, or does he work for the redeemer until the money is paid back? רבי יוסי הגלילי says relatives free him and others make him work. רבי עקיבא says the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: To freedom: the slave goes completely free
To work: the slave now works for the one who redeemed him
By any other person (not a relative)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. רבי יוסי הגלילי: relatives mean freedom. רבי עקיבא: relatives mean work. Each one is the reverse of the other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and Rabbi Akiva.
As it is taught: "He is not redeemed by any of these"
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
"By these" (relatives), it is to freedom,
by anyone else, it is to servitude.
Rabbi Akiva says:
"By these", it is to servitude,
by anyone else, it is to freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא, who use ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ to decide whether the redeemed slave goes free or works for the redeemer.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי הגלילי's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יוסי הגלילי gets his view from in the פסוק. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave only the two rulings. Now the גמרא wants to see how each one is read out of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the opinion quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יוסי הגלילי reads his view out of the פסוק.

steps.title: Two ways to read ״אִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל בְּאֵלֶּה״
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads it as 'if not redeemed by these but by another, he leaves only at יובל'. רבי עקיבא reads it as 'if not redeemed except by these, he leaves only at יובל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "If he is not redeemed by these", but by someone else, "then he goes out in the יובל year." And רבי עקיבא says: "If he is not redeemed" except "by these", "then he goes out in the יובל year."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how each תנא splits the same פסוק differently to get his own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, a slave redeemed by an outsider stays bound until יובל, so outsiders mean work and relatives mean freedom. For רבי עקיבא, the slave who stays bound until יובל is the one redeemed only by relatives, so relatives mean work and outsiders mean freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: By someone else
The fiftieth year, when slaves go free

phrases.english: The verse states: "If he is not redeemed by these"
but by another,
phrases.notes: These words are not in the פסוק. This is how רבי יוסי הגלילי fills it in.

phrases.english: "then he shall go out in the Jubilee Year."
And Rabbi Akiva says: "If he is not redeemed"
except "by these,"
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא reads 'only' into the פסוק, so it means: if he was redeemed only by relatives.

phrases.english: "then he shall go out in the Jubilee Year."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא אִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל בְּאֵלֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 and also gives רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each reads ״אִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל בְּאֵלֶּה״ with a different word added: 'but by another' or 'except by these'.

steps.title: The פסוק does not say 'only by these'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי objects to רבי עקיבא's reading: the פסוק does not say 'only by these'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי? Does it say "only by these"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוסי הגלילי would attack רבי עקיבא's reading: the word 'only' is not in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's reading needed the word 'except' or 'only', which the פסוק does not have. That makes this explanation of רבי עקיבא hard to accept, and it pushes the גמרא to look for a different basis for the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (meaning: it is not written)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?
phrases.notes: This is short for: how would רבי יוסי הגלילי answer רבי עקיבא's reading?

phrases.english: Is it written "only by these"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's reading in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading of ״אִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל בְּאֵלֶּה״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reading adds the word 'only', which is not written in the פסוק.

steps.title: A new basis: three kinds of redemption in one פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the first explanation and says they argue about a different פסוק, which lists redemption by relatives, by himself, and by others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they argue about this פסוק: "Or his uncle or his uncle's son shall redeem him" is redemption by relatives. "Or if he becomes able" is redemption by himself. "And he is redeemed" is redemption by others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the argument, based on ויקרא 25:49. It first lays out the three kinds of redemption the פסוק lists. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֶלָּא shows the גמרא is dropping its first explanation. The order in the פסוק matters: relatives first, himself in the middle, others last. The next step will use this order.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue
Being redeemed by relatives
Redeeming himself with his own money
Being redeemed by other people

phrases.english: Rather, they disagree about this verse:
"Either his uncle or his uncle's son may redeem him"
this is redemption by relatives,
"or if he becomes rich" — this is redemption by himself,
phrases.notes: Literally 'if his hand reaches', meaning he can now afford to pay.

phrases.english: "and he is redeemed" — this is redemption by others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem of step 9 by moving the argument to a different פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument came from how each one splits ״אִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל בְּאֵלֶּה״.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument comes from the order of the three kinds of redemption in ויקרא 25:49.

steps.title: Read the middle case with what comes before or after
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי links self-redemption to the case before it (relatives), so relatives mean freedom. רבי עקיבא links it to the case after it (others), so others mean freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that a פסוק is explained by what comes before it. Compare redemption by relatives to redemption by himself: just as redeeming himself leads to freedom, so too redemption by relatives leads to freedom. רבי עקיבא holds that a פסוק is explained by what comes after it. Compare redemption by others to redemption by himself: just as redeeming himself leads to freedom, so too redemption by others leads to freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the new explanation. The two תנאים argue about whether the middle case (redeeming himself) is grouped with the case before it or the case after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a slave who redeems himself goes fully free. רבי יוסי הגלילי links that case to the one before it, so relatives also free him. רבי עקיבא links it to the one after it, so others free him, and relatives are left as redemption to work.

keyTerms.meaning: A phrase is explained together with what comes before it
A phrase is explained together with what comes after it
Throw, meaning compare one case to another

steps.whatToRemember: Redeeming himself always means freedom. רבי יוסי הגלילי links it backward to relatives, so relatives mean freedom. רבי עקיבא links it forward to others, so others mean freedom.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the גמרא's second attempt to explain the argument. It gives each side a reason based on which direction to read a פסוק. The next steps test it, and in step 15 the גמרא moves to a logic-based explanation instead.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds:
a verse is expounded with what precedes it,
cast redemption by relatives onto redemption by himself,
just as redemption by himself is to freedom,
so too redemption by relatives is to freedom.
And Rabbi Akiva holds:
a verse is expounded with what follows it,
cast redemption by others onto redemption by himself,
just as redemption by himself is to freedom,
so too redemption by others is to freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי סָבַר מִקְרָא נִדְרָשׁ לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the three kinds of redemption from step 10 to explain each opinion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: At this stage the גמרא suggests the argument depends on whether the middle case in ויקרא 25:49 is read with the case before it (רבי יוסי הגלילי) or the case after it (רבי עקיבא). Later (step 15) the גמרא moves the argument to logic instead.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need the word ״באלה״?
steps.stepSummary: If the argument is only about whether self-redemption links to the case before it or after it, the word ״באלה״ seems to add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the word ״באלה״, "by these"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the new explanation from step 11. If the argument comes from linking the cases in the פסוק, what job is left for the word ״באלה״?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, ״באלה״ was the key word of the argument. After step 11 moved the argument to a different פסוק, ״באלה״ seems to have no role for either תנא. The גמרא wants to know what that word teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you just said is true
Why do I need it? (asks what a word or law adds)
By these; the word in the פסוק about redeeming the slave

phrases.english: If so,
why do I need "by these"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the explanation in step 11 by asking what the word ״באלה״ now teaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word ״באלה״ teaches, now that the argument rests on linking the cases in the earlier פסוק.

steps.title: Without ״באלה״ every redemption would bring freedom
steps.stepSummary: Without ״באלה״ we would link self-redemption to both cases, and every redemption would set him free. ״באלה״ limits freedom to only one kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for ״באלה״, I would have said that a פסוק is explained together with what comes before it and what comes after it, and every redemption leads to freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״באלה״ is a limiting word. It stops us from saying that every kind of redemption sets the slave free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a פסוק can be linked both to what comes before it and to what comes after it. Then redemption by relatives and redemption by others would both lead to freedom. ״באלה״ tells us that only one of them does, and each תנא picks which one.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said; what we would think without this source
A פסוק is explained together with what comes before it and after it
Freedom; the slave goes free

phrases.english: If not for "by these," I would have said

phrases.aramaic: מִקְרָא נִדְרָשׁ בֵּין לְפָנָיו בֵּין לְאַחֲרָיו,
phrases.english: a verse is explained both with what is before it and with what is after it,
and every redemption is to freedom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by giving ״באלה״ a limiting job.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״באלה״ stops us from linking self-redemption both ways. Only one kind of redemption leads to freedom.

steps.title: The old difficulty against רבי עקיבא comes back
steps.stepSummary: If ״באלה״ really matters, then the objection from step 9 returns. The פסוק says "by these," not "only by these."
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the difficulty goes back to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that its last answer brings back the earlier problem with רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once ״באלה״ decides the law again, we have to read it carefully. Its plain meaning, "if not redeemed by these," fits רבי יוסי הגלילי. רבי עקיבא needs "only by these," and the פסוק does not say that, which was the objection in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty or challenge
The difficulty goes back to its place; the old challenge is alive again

phrases.english: If so,
the difficulty goes back to its place.
phrases.notes: This is the objection from step 9: the פסוק does not say "only by these."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 13 brings back the challenge of step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״באלה״ decides the law, its plain meaning matches רבי יוסי הגלילי. The extra word "only" that רבי עקיבא needs is not in the פסוק.

steps.title: They argue based on logic: רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason
steps.stepSummary: The argument is not about reading the פסוק but about logic. רבי יוסי הגלילי says that if strangers' redemption brought freedom, nobody would redeem him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they argue about logic. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds: it makes sense that redemption by others leads to being bound to them, because if you say it leads to freedom, they would hold back and not redeem him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new approach: the two תנאים disagree because of logic, not because of the words of the פסוק. It starts with רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strangers lose their money if the slave they redeem goes free, so they would not redeem him. That is why רבי יוסי הגלילי says he works for them until יובל. This matches his ruling in step 6, that redemption by relatives brings freedom while redemption by others leads to servitude.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic; reasoning
They disagree
It makes sense; it stands to reason
Being bound in service; staying a slave
Redemption by other people who are not relatives

steps.confusionAlert: Here "לשיעבוד" does not mean he goes back to the non-Jew. It means he now serves the person who redeemed him, until יובל.

phrases.english: Rather, they disagree about logic:
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds:
it makes sense that redemption by others is to servitude,
because if you say it is to freedom,
they would hold back and not redeem him.
phrases.notes: Strangers would lose their money for nothing, so they would not pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by moving the argument from reading the פסוק to logic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the source of the argument from reading the פסוק to logic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument came from how to read the פסוק (״באלה״ or linking the cases).
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument comes from logic about what makes people act. For רבי יוסי הגלילי, strangers would not redeem him if he went free.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's logic: the slave would keep selling himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says that if redemption by relatives brought freedom, the slave would sell himself again and again, counting on his family to free him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds: it makes sense that redemption by relatives leads to being bound to them, because if you say it leads to freedom, every single day he would go and sell himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the new approach by giving רבי עקיבא's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא worries about the slave, not about the redeemers. If relatives always set him free, he could sell himself again and again, knowing his family will pay. So relatives' redemption leads to servitude, and redemption by others brings freedom, as in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption by relatives
Every single day
Sells himself

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים argue from logic. רבי יוסי הגלילי: strangers would not redeem him if he went free, so only relatives' redemption frees him. רבי עקיבא: he would keep selling himself if relatives freed him, so only strangers' redemption frees him.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds:
it makes sense that redemption by relatives is to servitude,
because if you say it is to freedom,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יוֹמָא וְיוֹמָא אֲזַל וּמְזַבֵּין נַפְשֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: every single day he would go and sell himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: מִסְתַּבְּרָא גְּאוּלַּת קְרוֹבִים לְשִׁיעְבּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the logic answer by giving רבי עקיבא's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second half of the logic answer
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא's position rests on the worry that the slave would misuse his relatives' help, not on the word ״באלה״.

steps.title: The חכמים say every redemption leads to freedom
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the two views belong only to רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא. The חכמים hold that every redemption sets the slave free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this is the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא, but the חכמים say every redemption leads to freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a new statement: a third group, the חכמים, disagrees with both תנאים. The next steps identify who these חכמים are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא hold that some redemptions bind the slave to the redeemer. The חכמים reject that and say any redemption, by relatives, by himself, or by others, sets him free.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the view of
The Sages; the majority view
Every redemption leads to freedom

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. רבי יוסי הגלילי: only relatives' redemption frees him. רבי עקיבא: only others' redemption frees him. חכמים: every redemption frees him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the whole argument between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא is not the only view, because the חכמים disagree with both of them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: this is the view of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and Rabbi Akiva,
but the Sages say: every redemption is to freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two תנאים' reasons are explained, this adds the third view, that of the חכמים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים hold that a Jewish slave redeemed from a non-Jew always goes free, whoever redeems him.

steps.title: Who are the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the חכמים are that hold every redemption frees the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are these חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which specific תנא is behind the view of the חכמים that רבי יוחנן just mentioned. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the חכמים disagree with both רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא. Now the גמרא wants a name, so it can explain how that view handles the word ״בְּאֵלֶּה״.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?
The Sages, the majority view

phrases.english: Who are the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The חכמים from רבי יוחנן's statement just before this, who say every redemption sets the slave free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the חכמים mentioned in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the view of the חכמים?

steps.title: The חכמים are רבי, who reads the פסוק in both directions
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are רבי. He uses ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ for a different teaching, and he reads the פסוק as connected to what comes before it and after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי. He takes the word ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ for a different teaching. He also holds that a פסוק is explained by what comes before it and by what comes after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים are רבי, and it explains why he does not limit freedom to one kind of redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא, ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ limited freedom to only one kind of redemption. רבי uses that word for something else, so nothing limits the rule. Because he reads the פסוק as linked to both the case before it (redemption by relatives) and the case after it (redemption by others), both kinds of redemption set the slave free.

keyTerms.meaning: He takes it out, meaning he uses it for another purpose
A different teaching

keyTerms.term: מִקְרָא נִדְרָשׁ בֵּין לְפָנָיו וּבֵין לְאַחֲרָיו
keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק is explained by what comes before it and by what comes after it

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים are רבי. Since ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ is used for something else, and the פסוק connects in both directions, every redemption frees the slave.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי does not ignore ״בְּאֵלֶּה״. He agrees the word teaches something. He just uses it for a different teaching than limiting freedom.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi],
who takes this word "by these"
for a different teaching,
and [he holds that] a verse is explained
both by what is before it and by what is after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי הִיא, דְּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְהַאי ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ לִדְרָשָׁה אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 and explains how the חכמים read the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי. He uses ״בְּאֵלֶּה״ for another teaching and reads the פסוק as connected in both directions, so every redemption frees the slave.

steps.title: What does רבי learn from ״וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי does with the words ״וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, what does he do with the words ״וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what teaching רבי takes from the words "then he shall go out in the יובל year." This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the גמרא has explained how רבי reads ״בְּאֵלֶּה״, it checks the rest of the פסוק. It wants to know what job these words do in רבי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (What does he learn from it?)
The יובל year, every 50th year

phrases.english: And Rabbi, this phrase "then he shall go out in the Jubilee Year,"
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי, הַאי ״וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי's reading from step 19 by asking about another phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What teaching does רבי learn from ״וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל״?

steps.title: רבי needs it for a teaching in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי needs the phrase for a teaching from a ברייתא, and it begins quoting that ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא: ״וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבי uses these words for a teaching found in a ברייתא. It starts quoting the ברייתא, and the rest of it continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is not extra for רבי. It carries its own teaching. Here the גמרא only quotes the opening words of the ברייתא, so the actual teaching comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a specific teaching)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught [in a baraita]:
"Then he shall go out in the Jubilee Year"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 20 by citing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי uses ״וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל״ for a teaching taught in a ברייתא, which the גמרא begins to quote.
